title: Summary, review and chapter test
competency: Review the unit and take the timed chapter test.

keywords.def: A perennial, edible plant grown for its true botanical fruit or products made from it.

en.text: Fruits are nutritious, raise household income and food security and can support the national economy; Ethiopia has diverse climate, water and labour, though lack of knowledge has limited production. Fruits are classified by structure, temperature requirement, ripening and plant type. They are propagated by seed or vegetatively, each with advantages and disadvantages. Nurseries and orchards need careful planning, correct spacing and good irrigation, and harvest and postharvest handling decide fruit quality. Floriculture is a growing export sector.

screens.text: Which storage temperature suits apples but would damage bananas?
screens.why: Apples (temperate) keep near 0 °C; bananas (tropical) get chilling injury below about 13 °C.

screens.ask: Lemons are planted 6 m × 5 m. Trees per hectare = ___ (nearest whole tree)

screens.text: A highland school (cold, frosty winters, sandy soil, little water) wants a fruit garden. Which plan fits the unit best?
opts: Grafted apple trees, drip irrigation, nursery seedlings in poly-bags
Banana suckers, basin irrigation on sandy soil
screens.ans: Grafted apple trees, drip irrigation, nursery seedlings in poly-bags
screens.why: Apple is temperate (needs cold); grafting keeps the variety; drip saves water and suits sandy soil; bags protect the tap root.
screens.clue: Check crop, propagation and irrigation one at a time.

items.text: Which of the following is among the problems of fruit crop production and management?

Lack of storage and transportation facilities

items.title: Project 2.1: order the steps for a school fruit garden
items: Choose a gently sloping, well-drained site near water
Fill poly-bags with 2:1:1 mix and sow viable seed
Water, shade and weed; discard weak seedlings
Dig holes, keep topsoil apart, mix it with manure
Plant at the right spacing without bending the tap root
Irrigate in the morning and record growth
items.why: Site → nursery → care → holes → planting → management.
items.clue: Seedlings must be raised before planting out.

notes.text: Review Part II Q2 "Steam" → Stem; Q6 "ango" → Mango; Q8 option A "flat" → gently sloping; the second "Part II" should be Part III.

Review Q5 (papaya "only propagated by" A. Seeds B. Sexual propagation D. A and B) has two equal correct options and "only" is too strong; reworded as "normally propagated by: seed / grafting / cuttings / suckers".
Review Q9 has overlapping options (B and D both "energy") and a weak "None" key; kept as printed. Q10 options A, B and E are not stated in the unit and must be reasoned.
The unit summary omits irrigation, postharvest and floriculture. Part III short answers are turned into pick, order and sort items. The lemon spacing item and the school garden challenge are added.
